quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly while in a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Straighten the handlebars, then stop.
Apply both brakes suddenly while still leaning.
Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten the handlebars, then stop.
questions.explanation: First straighten your motorcycle and square the handlebars, then stop. If you cannot straighten up, apply the brakes smoothly and gradually. Reduce your lean angle and increase brake pressure as you slow down.

questions.question: A dog is chasing your motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Swerve around the dog.
Stop and wait for the dog to lose interest.
Ride next to the dog.
Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Downshift and ride slowly toward the dog. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: When riding in rain or fog, what headlights should you use?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight.
Use your low beam headlight.
Do not use your headlight.
Switch between low and high beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlight.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in rain, snow, or fog. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: Your front wheel skids because you braked too hard. What should you do?

options.text: Keep pressing the front brake.
Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks up from braking, release the front brake immediately and apply it again smoothly.

questions.question: How can you prevent other vehicles from trying to share your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Swerve back and forth in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage car drivers from trying to share your space.

questions.question: When turning, where should you look?

options.text: Turn both your head and shoulders.
Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Use only your mirrors.
Move only your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look toward where you want to go through the turn. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Should motorcycle riders wear hearing protection?

options.text: Yes, wear it all the time to prevent hearing damage.
Only wear it on long rides.
No, it blocks important sounds like horns and sirens.
No, a helmet is enough protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, wear it all the time to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can cause permanent hearing damage, even with a full-face helmet. Ear plugs provide protection while still letting you hear important sounds.

questions.question: How do motorcycle stopping distances compare to car stopping distances?

options.text: Cars need much longer to stop.
Cars need slightly longer to stop.
Motorcycles need longer to stop.
They stop in about the same distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: They stop in about the same distance.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, motorcycles and cars stop in nearly the same distance. However, wet or slippery pavement makes it much harder for motorcycles to stop quickly.

questions.question: In a slow, tight turn, how should the rider position their body?

options.text: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
Lean at the same angle as the motorcycle.
Lean in the opposite direction of the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright while your body leans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, lean with your motorcycle. In slow, tight turns, keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which instruction should you NOT give them?

options.text: Get on after the engine starts.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.
Hold firmly to your waist, hips, or belt.
Feel free to talk whenever they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel free to talk whenever they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should stay quiet and still so you can focus on riding. They should get on only after the engine starts, sit as far forward as possible without crowding you, and hold firmly to your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: How should a rider sit to best control a motorcycle?

options.text: With arms fully extended.
Using arms to hold their body up.
With knees away from the gas tank.
With feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: With feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Use your arms to control the motorcycle, not to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet firmly on the footrests to maintain balance.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists ride when entering a highway or curve?

options.text: Single-file.
In a staggered formation.
In pairs.
In the far right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file.
questions.explanation: While staggered formation is usually best, switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: What does the lead rider signal when they raise their left arm and extend their index finger?

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Move to single-file formation.
The group will exit at the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Hand signals help group riders communicate. When the lead rider raises their left arm and extends their index finger, the group should move into a single-file formation.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane when being passed from behind?

options.text: In the center portion of the lane.
In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center portion of your lane when being passed. This discourages the other driver from returning to your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: What does it mean when an operator's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward?

options.text: Planning to turn left.
About to stop.
Planning to turn right.
About to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Planning to turn right.
questions.explanation: Operators use hand signals instead of mechanical turn signals. When the left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, it means the operator plans to turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: Should you use your headlight during the day?

options.text: No.
Yes, on high beam.
Yes, on low beam.
Yes, alternating between high and low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, on high beam.
questions.explanation: Using high beam during the day helps other drivers see you. Use your high beam headlight any time you are not riding behind or approaching other vehicles.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on a motorcycle?

options.text: As low as possible
As high as possible
Behind the rear axle
On one side of the motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them or use saddlebags. Piling loads high on the back can raise the motorcycle's center of gravity and affect balance. Distribute loads equally on both sides of the motorcycle.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance when riding a motorcycle at night?

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.
Five seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see and judge distances. Keep at least three seconds of following distance. You may need extra time to realize the vehicle ahead has stopped and to avoid hitting it.

questions.question: What does this signal mean?

options.text: Rest stop
High beams on
Turn right
Hazard

questions.correctAnswerText: Hazard
questions.explanation: Group riders use signals to communicate. When the lead rider extends their right leg, it means there is a hazard in the roadway on the right side.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Help you see better.
Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Give you an escape route if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should keep you away from blind spots and hazards. Your position should discourage sharing your lane and provide an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Leave the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a wet lane is dangerous. When rain starts, ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is usually the best choice.

questions.question: How do you do maximum straight-line braking?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: Maximum braking in a straight line means using both the front and rear brakes together without locking either wheel.

questions.question: Why should you not change gears on railroad tracks?

options.text: Your motorcycle may stall.
You might go too fast.
Other drivers may not expect you to shift gears.
The uneven surface makes shifting harder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may stall.
questions.explanation: Do not shift gears when crossing railroad tracks. Your motorcycle could stall while on the tracks.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, EXCEPT:

options.text: Help you see and be seen.
Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Avoid hazards on the road surface.
Block your access to an escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block your access to an escape route.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should keep you away from blind spots and hazards. Your position should discourage sharing your lane and provide an escape route if danger appears.
